He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier Musketeers]]. After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Marshall signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He played for the Pelicans for four years before signing with the Mavericks as a free agent in 2024. ==Early life== Marshall was born in [[Atlantic City, New Jersey]] but moved to Maryland at the age of 9.{{cite news |last1=McGarry |first1=Mike |title=Naji Marshall – An NBA and Atlantic City success story |url=https://pressofatlanticcity.com/naji-marshall---an-nba-and-atlantic-city-success-story/article_8a75c5a8-eaaf-11eb-abf0-1373d067865d.html |access-date=November 6, 2021 |work=[[Press of Atlantic City]] |date=July 26, 2021}} He is the son of Maurice Marshall, who was a professional boxer and is now a basketball coach at an elementary school, and Rayna Whitted, who works at [[Providence Hospital (Washington, D.C.)|Providence Hospital]] in Washington, D.C. His name means "strong warrior" in Arabic and was a nickname of his father's. Marshall has five brothers and one sister and grew up playing football and basketball.{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=The quiet confidence of Naji Marshall: Is he Xavier basketball's next big star? |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/xaviersports/2018/10/03/xavier-basketball-naji-marshall-next-big-star-quiet-confidence/1486840002/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=October 3, 2018}} In middle school, he played in Atlantic City's Triple-B summer youth league. He played his first season of high school basketball at [[Takoma Academy]]. As a sophomore, he transferred to [[Eleanor Roosevelt High School (Maryland)|Eleanor Roosevelt High School]] to play under coach Brendan O'Connell but was academically ineligible his first year. As a senior, Marshall averaged 17 [[Point (basketball)|points]], nine [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], four [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and two [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game. He led Eleanor Roosevelt to a 23–3 record and scored 27 points to lead the Raiders past [[Perry Hall High School]] 69–59, in the Maryland 4A state semifinals. He decided to attend the [[Hargrave Military Academy]] as a [[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] student to improve his academics.{{cite news |last1=Giannotto |first1=Mark |title=Naji Marshall's maturation on and off the court sparks Eleanor Roosevelt's title quest |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/naji-marshalls-maturation-on-and-off-the-court-sparks-eleanor-roosevelts-title-quest/2016/03/11/3548ecb0-e7a7-11e5-a6f3-21ccdbc5f74e_story.html |access-date=November 18, 2019 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date=March 11, 2016}} Marshall averaged 20.7 points and 11.4 rebounds per game at Hargrave Military Academy.{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Shannon |title=Family focus: Tight-knit relationships at home and Xavier mold Naji Marshall |url=https://theathletic.com/1265918/2019/10/04/family-focus-tight-knit-relationships-at-home-and-xavier-mold-naji-marshall/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191229200216/https://theathletic.com/1265918/2019/10/04/family-focus-tight-knit-relationships-at-home-and-xavier-mold-naji-marshall/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 29, 2019 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=October 9, 2019}} He competed for DC Premier on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit. Marshall received scholarship offers from [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], but committed to playing college basketball for [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] because he liked the culture. He was considered to be a four-star prospect by three recruiting sites, and ESPN ranked him as the 20th best small forward in his class. ==College career== Marshall contributed 12 points and four rebounds in his collegiate opening game against [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]].{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Shannon |title=Russell: Freshman Naji Marshall has made an instant impact for the Xavier Musketeers |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/russell-freshman-naji-marshall-has-made-an-instant-impact-for-the-xavier-musketeers |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=WCPO |date=January 17, 2018}} He scored a season-high 21 points in a 89–77 win over [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] on February 21, 2018.{{cite news |title=Marshall helps No. 4 Xavier beat Georgetown 89–77 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988620 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 21, 2018}} Marshall was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman team.{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-xaviers-bluiett-villanovas-brunson-butlers-martin-unanimously-named-all-big-east.aspx |title=Xavier's Bluiett, Villanova's Brunson, Butler's Martin Unanimously Named All-Big East |publisher=[[Big East Conference]] |date=March 4, 2018 |access-date=November 18, 2019}} As a freshman, Marshall averaged 7.7 points and 4.4 rebounds per game and made 18 starts. In the summer before his sophomore season, Marshall worked on improving his [[jump shot (basketball)|jump shot]] and his conditioning. Marshall earned his first Big East player of the week honors on December 31, 2018, after scoring 19 points, grabbing a career-high 14 rebounds, and dished out four assists in a 74–65 win against [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]].{{cite web |title=Xavier's Marshall, Georgetown's LeBlanc Earn MBB Weekly Honors |url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2018/12/31/mens-basketball-xaviers-marshall-georgetowns-leblanc-earn-mbb-weekly-honors.aspx |website=Big East Conference |access-date=November 19, 2019 |date=December 31, 2018}} After scoring 28 points in a win at [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] on February 20, 2019, and recording 17 points in a win over [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] on February 24, Marshall was again named Big East player of the week.{{cite news |title=Xavier's Marshall named Big East Conference Player of the Week |url=https://local12.com/sports/xu-musketeers/xaviers-marshall-named-big-east-conference-player-of-the-week-xavier-musketeers-bigeast-ncaa-college-basketball-cincinnati |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=WKRC |date=February 25, 2019}} On February 28, Marshall scored a career-high 31 points as Xavier defeated [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] 84–73.{{cite news |title=Marshall scores 31 to lift Xavier over St. John's 84–73 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/02/28/marshall-scores-31-to-lift-xavier-over-st-johns-84-73/39133309/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 28, 2019}} Marshall missed a game against St. John's with an ankle injury on March 9. He was named to the Second Team All-Big East by the coaches as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=Xavier Musketeers forward Naji Marshall named All-Big East Conference second team |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/xaviersports/2019/03/10/xavier-musketeers-star-naji-marshall-named-all-big-east-second-team/3123270002/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=March 10, 2019}} Marshall averaged 14.7 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, shooting 39.4 percent from the field and 27.7 percent from behind the arc. After the season, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but withdrew his name and returned to Xavier.{{cite news |last1=Broering |first1=Rick |title=Naji Marshall withdraws from NBA Draft, will return to Xavier |url=https://247sports.com/college/xavier/Article/Naji-Marshall-withdraws-from-NBA-Draft-and-returns-to-Xavier-Musketeers-for-junior-season-in-2019-20-131805723/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=May 5, 2019}} Coming into his junior season, Marshall was named to the preseason First Team All-Big East and was on the watchlist for the [[Julius Erving Award]].{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=Xavier's Naji Marshall, Tyrique Jones named to national award watch lists |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/xaviersports/2019/10/18/xaviers-naji-marshall-tyrique-jones-named-national-award-lists/4023230002/ |access-date=November 18, 2019 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=October 18, 2019}} On December 7, Marshall tied his career-high of 31 points in a 73–66 win over [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] in the [[Crosstown Shootout]].{{cite news |title=Marshall scores 31, Xavier beats rival Cincinnati 73–66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169457 |access-date=December 9, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 7, 2019}} He sat out a game against [[Western Carolina Catamounts|Western Carolina]] on December 18 with a stomach virus.{{cite news |last1=Hall |first1=Eric |title=Xavier leading scorer Naji Marshall not playing vs. Western Carolina basketball |url=https://www.citizen-times.com/story/sports/2019/12/18/xaviers-naji-marshall-not-playing-wcu-catamounts-basketball-western-carolina/2692885001/ |access-date=December 29, 2019 |work=[[Asheville Citizen Times]] |date=December 18, 2019}} On February 1, 2020, Marshall contributed 19 points, 10 rebounds and four assists in a 74–62 upset of tenth-ranked Seton Hall despite playing with the flu.{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title='Not MJ bad, but you know': Xavier star Naji Marshall played through the flu at Seton Hall |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/02/01/not-mj-bad-xaviers-naji-marshall-played-flu-seton-hall/4633851002/ |access-date=March 1, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=February 1, 2020}} Marshall hit the game-winning three-pointer with 4.5 seconds left in a 66–63 win at [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] on March 1, finishing with 20 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite news |title=Marshall's 3-pointer gives Xavier win over Georgetown 66–63 |url=https://local12.com/sports/xu-musketeers/marshalls-3-pointer-gives-xavier-win-over-georgetown-66-63 |access-date=March 2, 2020 |work=WKRC |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 1, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Marshall was named to the First Team All-Big East.{{cite news |last1=Baum |first1=Adam |title=Xavier basketball players honored on All-Big East Conference teams |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/03/08/xavier-basketball-gets-4-players-all-conference-team/4994440002/ |access-date=March 8, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=March 8, 2020}} He averaged 16.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=Russell |first1=Shannon |title=Looking ahead to Xavier's Team 99 after an abrupt ending to the season |url=https://theathletic.co.uk/1674568/2020/03/13/looking-ahead-to-xaviers-team-99-after-an-abrupt-ending-to-the-season/ |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=March 13, 2020}} Following the season, Marshall declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Baum|first1=Adam|title=Report: Xavier's Naji Marshall has declared for the 2020 NBA Draft|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/03/26/report-xaviers-naji-marshall-has-declared-2020-nba-draft/2914759001/|work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]]|access-date=March 30, 2020|date=March 26, 2020}} On April 9, he announced he was signing with an agent, thus forgoing his remaining season of collegiate eligibility. Marshall scored 1,277 points in three seasons as a Musketeer.{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Pat |title=Naji Marshall's Xavier basketball career is over after he signs with an agent |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2020/04/09/naji-marshalls-xavier-basketball-career-over/5125106002/ |access-date=May 9, 2020 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=April 9, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Pelicans (2020–2024)=== After going unselected in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Marshall signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]] on December 8, 2020.{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign Naji Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-naji-marshall |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=December 8, 2020}} On January 15, 2021, Marshall made his NBA debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |last1=Trahan |first1=Ken |title=Pelicans blown away by Lakers despite early 15-point lead |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/highlights-pelicans-blown-away-by-lakers-despite-early-15-point-lead/ |website=Crescent City Sports |access-date=November 6, 2021 |date=January 15, 2021}} He began receiving consistent minutes in April due to a rash of injuries to players. On May 7, 2021, the Pelicans signed him to a multi-year contract.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Naji Marshall|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-naji-marshall-050721|date=May 7, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 7, 2021}} In his rookie season, Marshall averaged 7.7 points and 4.6 rebounds per game for the Pelicans, shooting 39.2 percent from the field.{{cite news |last1=Rude |first1=Jacob |title=2020–21 New Orleans Pelicans Player Review: Naji Marshall |url=https://lonzowire.usatoday.com/2021/06/08/2020-21-new-orleans-pelicans-player-review-naji-marshall/ |access-date=November 6, 2021 |work=Lonzo Wire |date=June 8, 2021}} In January 2022, he and [[Trey Murphy III]] were assigned to the Pelicans' [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite news |title=New Orleans Pelicans Assign Naji Marshall and Trey Murphy Iii to Birmingham Squadron |url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/new-orleans-pelicans-assign-naji-marshall-and-trey-murphy-iii-to-birmingham-squadron/ |access-date=January 24, 2022 |work=Nola.com |date=January 22, 2022}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2024–present)=== On July 6, 2024, Marshall signed a three-year, $27 million contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=MAVERICKS ADD MARSHALL TO SOFTEN LOSS OF JONES|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-add-naji-marshall/|website=Mavs.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}} On December 28, 2024, Marshall was suspended for 4 games after an altercation with [[Jusuf Nurkić]].{{cite web | title=NBA announces penalties from Mavericks-Suns game | website=NBA Communications | date=December 28, 2024 | url=https://pr.nba.com/mavericks-suns-suspensions/ | access-date=December 7, 2025}} On March 25, 2025, Marshall scored a career-high 38 points along with seven rebounds in a 128–113 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Curtis|title=Despite Naji Marshall's offensive eruption, Mavericks run out of gas at MSG vs. Knicks|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2025/03/25/despite-naji-marshalls-offensive-eruption-mavericks-run-out-of-gas-at-msg-vs-knicks/ |website=The Dallas Morning News |date=March 26, 2025 |access-date=March 26, 2025}} On August 2, 2026, the Mavericks announced that they had re-signed Marshall to a multi-year contract extension but did not disclose the details.{{citeweb|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mavericks-sign-forward-naji-marshall-to-contract-extension|title=Mavericks sign forward Naji Marshall to contract extension|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=August 2, 2026|accessdate=August 2, 2026}} The same day, [[ESPN]] reported that Marshall had agreed to a three–year, $52 million extension.{{citeweb|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49514965/sources-mavs-extend-naji-marshall-3-year-522m-deal|title=Sources: Mavs extend Naji Marshall on 3-year, $52.2M
